item.title: aadd
item.description:
## The Problem Modern speech‑processing pipelines generate thousands of audio files that may contain noise, clipping, codec artefacts, or other degradations. Manually listening to each file is infeasible. AADD supplies a fast, frame‑level classifier that reports *which* degradation is present and *where*, enabling automatic quality gating for ASR/TTS training or post‑processing validation.

item.title: Vision Agents
item.description:
## The Problem
Real-time video AI agents are hard to build because the pipeline spans video ingestion, object detection, speech, and an LLM, and each hop adds latency. Most frameworks treat video as an afterthought or lock you into one model provider. This repo solves that by giving you a Python core that wires video/audio tracks, vision processors (YOLO, Roboflow), and pluggable LLM/STT/TTS providers together over Stream's low-latency edge network, with a claimed sub-30ms audio/video path.

item.title: substrate
item.description:
## The Problem Running many autonomous agents on shared Kubernetes clusters requires isolation that standard containers cannot provide. Agents are idle most of the time, so containers waste memory, and untrusted code can access credentials if a pod is compromised. A runtime that can snapshot idle agents and resume them quickly while keeping each agent in its own micro‑VM is needed.

item.title: all agentic architectures
item.description:
## The Problem
Modern agentic systems often struggle with the reliability of LLM-as-scorer mechanisms, where probabilistic free-text outputs lead to inconsistent agent behavior—colloquially known as the "flat-band pathology." This repository addresses that instability by implementing a deterministic-picker pattern, requiring LLMs to commit to categorical features (booleans, enums) rather than unstructured scores, allowing Python to compose the final decision signal.

item.title: bashkit
item.description:
**The Problem** Applications that need to run user‑supplied shell scripts must isolate those scripts from the host process, the real file system, and the network. A typical approach spawns a new process, which is expensive and fragile in multi‑tenant or serverless environments. The goal here is to provide a pure‑Rust, in‑process bash interpreter that offers POSIX‑level features while guaranteeing isolation and controllable resource limits.
